title: Projectile Angle Explorer
tagline: Discover why 45° travels farthest on flat ground
core_question: Why does a 45-degree launch angle make a projectile travel farther on flat ground than other angles?
payoff: You can predict the best angle by seeing how the horizontal speed and the time of flight trade off against each other, then test it with sliders.
running_example: A projectile launched at exactly 20 m/s from ground level on flat ground, with g = 10 m/s²; we test angles 30°, 45°, and 60° and read the range each time.

parameters.label: Launch speed
parameters.description: Initial speed (fixed at 20 m/s in examples)

phases.title: See the default flight
phases.coach: Watch the projectile launched at 45° with speed 20 m/s. Notice the green horizontal arrow and blue vertical arrow at launch.
phases.hint: Just watch the path and readouts.
phases.success: You see the curved path and current range.

phases.title: Change the angle
phases.coach: Move only the angle slider. Watch how the green arrow shortens while the blue arrow lengthens.
phases.success: You observed the trade-off between horizontal and vertical speed.

phases.title: Predict the winner
phases.coach: Before testing, decide which angle will give the longest red range arrow.

quiz.prompt: At which angle do you expect the longest range?

choices.text: 45° because horizontal and vertical effects balance
60° because time in air is longest

quiz.explanation: The product of horizontal speed and flight time peaks at 45°.

phases.hint: Think about the green and gray lengths multiplying.

phases.title: Test your prediction
phases.coach: Unlock the slider and try 30°, 45°, and 60°. Watch the red range arrow.
phases.success: 45° indeed gives the longest range; 30° and 60° match each other.

phases.title: Hit the target
phases.coach: Adjust angle and speed until the projectile lands inside the target zone at 40 m.
phases.success: You hit the target by balancing the two speeds.

phases.title: Check the trade-off
phases.coach: Answer using what you just saw with the arrows.

quiz.prompt: Why does range drop again after 45° even though flight time keeps rising?

choices.text: Horizontal speed shrinks faster than flight time grows
The projectile starts to curve backward

quiz.explanation: The shrinking green arrow wins over the growing gray bar past 45°.

phases.hint: Look at the green arrow length versus the gray bar.

phases.title: Name the payoff
phases.coach: You now see that range is the product of constant horizontal speed and total flight time; their best balance is at 45°.
phases.success: You can predict the longest-range angle without guessing.

misconceptions: A higher launch always travels farther because it stays in the air longer.
The angle for maximum height is also the angle for maximum range.
